newsitem.title: USA: U.S., EU planning further meat talks next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S., EU planning further meat talks next week.

text.p: The United States and the European Union are planning to continue negotiations next week on meat inspection regulations in a last ditch attempt to avert a damaging trade war, said the Agriculture Department's senior trade adviser Paul Drazek on Wednesday.

"We're counting on the next talks being (held) next week," Drazek told reporters in a briefing held one day after the United States and the EU announced separate actions that could halt the bilateral trade of hundreds of millions of dollars worth of poultry and meat products.

The inability of U.S. and EU officials to reach agreement in the so-called veterinary equivalency talks by an April 1 deadline set into motion Tuesday actions by both sides that could halt the imports of European meat into the United States and stop U.S. poultry shipments from entering Europe.
Washington announced Tuesday that as of April 15, European meat and poultry plants that cannot meet U.S. inspection standards will not be able to export to the United States.
Drazek said officials are going back to the table to try to come up with an agreement before April 15. "The next two weeks we will be trying very hard to get an agreement," he said.
Drazek said that with or without an agreement, there are still elements of the dispute that the United States could decide to take to the World Trade Organization.
"WTO is clearly an option...There are some things we are looking at right now as WTO issues," he said.

Drazek would not say when Washington will decide to pursue any of the issues under the auspices of WTO, but indicated it may be soon. "We wouldn't procrastinate" taking it to WTO once that decision is made, he said.
